title: Hybrid run-length prefix encoding and KV residency optimization
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background:
We see significant duplication in stored prompt prefixes across concurrent requests for long-chat workloads. Existing prefix dedupe strategies (fingerprinting + exact chunk coalescing) work well for byte-identical fragments but miss high-frequency near-duplicate sequences produced by small edits or templated prompts. On large tenants this causes wasted GPU KV residency and increases eviction churn, which in turn increases tail latency for cold requests.

Goal:
Design and implement a hybrid run-length encoding (RLE) + micro-fragment canonicalizer for prefix storage that reduces per-prefix memory by: (1) compactly encoding repeated token runs (useful for tokens like whitespace/punctuation or repeated system tokens), (2) representing small near-duplicate segments as canonical micro-fragments with similarity-hash identifiers, and (3) admitting residency hints for fragments to steer placement into GPU hotstore vs ephemeral slabs. The system should be compatible with continuous batching and not increase critical path latency.

Scope & Non-goals:
- In scope: on-path serialization format, admission policy for residency, background re-canonicalization job, metrics and rollout controls.
- Out of scope: cross-tenant encryption changes, large-model architectural kernel work, or changing runtime batching algorithm fundamentals.

Design proposal summary:
1) Encoding layer: when inserting a prefix into the shard store, run a lightweight RLE pass over token ids (thresholded run length > 4) to emit compressed tokens with an RLE opcode. RLE op uses <opcode, token, run_length> and reduces memory for repetitive scaffolding tokens common in prompt templates.
2) Micro-fragment canonicalizer: break prefixes into micro-fragments (16-64 token windows) and compute two fingerprints: a stable content-hash (xxh64) and a fuzzy similarity hash (sparse simhash). If a micro-fragment's simhash is within Hamming threshold to an existing canonical fragment, store a reference to canonical id instead of full token list. Canonical fragments are versioned and immutable.
3) KV residency hints: fragments are annotated with a residency score derived from recent access frequency and size. Scheduler uses residency score to place hot canonical fragments in GPU hotstore (longer-lived) and colder ones in ephemeral slab. Implement lightweight crediting to avoid immediate eviction during bursts.
4) Hybrid lookup at inference time: during KV lookup, assemble requested prefix by concatenating RLE-decoded segments and resolving canonical fragment references. Maintain a short decoding fast-path that avoids allocation by streaming into GPU prefetch buffers.

Compatibility & correctness:
- Decoding must be bit-exact to original token sequence. Compression is lossless.
- Canonical fragment references must include version/tombstone metadata so stale references are safe to ignore (fall back to full fragment retrieval).

Performance targets:
- Reduce median KV memory footprint per stored prefix by >= 22% for templated dialog workloads in benchmarks.
- Keep additional on-path decoding CPU cycles < 3 microseconds per fragment on p99 traffic (measured on our perf bench).
- Reduce eviction-induced cold-start latency p95 by 15% for baseline workloads.

Implementation plan (milestones):
M1 (2w): Prototype RLE encoder/decoder and micro-fragment splitter in Python. Add unit tests and simple simhash index.
M2 (3w): Implement C++-fastpath encoder/decoder and integrate with shard persistence layer. Add residency score field and basic placement policy.
M3 (2w): Background re-canonicalizer worker to merge similar fragments and compact storage.
M4 (2w): Integration with continuous batching hotstore prefetch path. End-to-end benchmarks and fallback safety tests.
M5 (1w): Gradual rollout via runtime feature flag and canary tenants.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for encoding/decoding, canonicalization, and versioned references.
- Stress bench: synthetic templated prompts (product-descriptions, long system templates) to validate memory reductions.
- Integration perf on canary cluster with tracing (token-level latency, GPU memory accounting).

Rollout and observation:
- Add dashboard: canonical-fragment-count, avg-fragment-size, RLE-compression-ratio, residency-hit-rate, decode-latency histogram.
- Start with small canary (internal tenants) for 48h, then subset of small customers, monitor p99 latency, evictions, and memory curves.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: simhash false positives cause excessive pointer indirections, increasing decode latency. Mitigation: tune Hamming threshold, prefer content-hash exact matches for references; instrument decode-path to fall back to inline token copy.
- Risk: background re-canonicalization can cause bursts of IO. Mitigation: rate-limit compaction jobs and perform during low-traffic windows.

Open questions:
- Optimal micro-fragment window size for our token distributions (bench across 16/32/64).
- Trade-off point between residency credit duration and eviction fairness for multi-tenant scenarios.

Success criteria (post-rollout):
- 20%+ KV mem reduction for templated prompts in production-like benchmarks.
- No measurable increase in user-observed generation latency (p50/p95).
- Reduced frequency of eviction-thrashing incidents for high-traffic tenants.
